items.fullSentence: J'ai oublié mon livre chez moi.
items.sentenceTrans: I left my book at home.

whyWrong.mes: mes is plural — one book takes mon.
whyWrong.sa: sa is feminine — livre is masculine (and sa means 'his/her', not 'my').
whyWrong.ma: livre is masculine — mon livre, not ma.

items.fullSentence: Je voudrais vous présenter ma famille.
items.sentenceTrans: I'd like to introduce my family.

whyWrong.mon: famille is feminine and starts with a consonant — ma famille.
whyWrong.mes: mes is plural — one family takes ma.

items.fullSentence: Pierre a posé son sac sur la chaise.
items.sentenceTrans: Pierre put his bag on the chair.

whyWrong.sa: sac is masculine — son sac, not sa.
whyWrong.ma: ma is feminine — sac is masculine (and it means 'my', not 'his').
whyWrong.ses: ses is plural — one bag takes son.

whyWrong.mon: mon is singular — clés is plural, so mes.
whyWrong.ma: ma is singular — clés is plural, so mes.

items.fullSentence: Je te présente mon amie Camille.
items.sentenceTrans: Let me introduce my friend Camille.

whyWrong.ma: amie starts with a vowel — ma becomes mon before it.
whyWrong.une: une is 'a', not a possessive — you need 'my'.

whyWrong.nos: nos is plural — one apartment takes notre.

items.fullSentence: Madame, montrez votre passeport, s'il vous plaît.

whyWrong.vos: vos is plural — one passport takes votre.
whyWrong.ton: ton is informal 'your' — with vous, use votre.

items.sentenceTrans: The students listen to their teacher.

whyWrong.leurs: leurs is plural — one teacher takes leur.
whyWrong.son: son is 'his/her' (one owner) — the students share, so leur.
whyWrong.ses: ses is plural (and one owner) — one shared teacher takes leur.
